messages:
maria: Heads-up: saw a spike in preemptible evictions in us-west1 yesterday, ~120 evictions in 10 min. A few live-stream requests were dropped.

alex: Oof. Any correlation with node reboots or GC? link: https://grafana.redwood/replicas/evictions?from=...

maria: no scheduled reboots. Spike matches cloud preemptible reclaim wave, looks like short notice (30-60s). Most fails happened during streaming kv prefix handoffs.

sam: We're seeing two problems: 1) requests holding long-lived streaming tokens get cut and aren't requeued cleanly, 2) KV cache not checkpointed so cutover loses prefix state, forcing full regen -> tail latency.

jen: Idea: lightweight keepalive ioctl to extend ephemeral lease by +15s when node sees an imminent preemptible signal, combined with async KV snapshot to GCS every N seconds. If keepalive fails, stream requeue occurs but with saved state to resume. Tradeoff: extra GCS ops and tiny cost vs lower user-visible errors.

maria: Draft config:
```
keepalive: { enabled: true, ttl_extend: 15 }
snapshot: { interval_sec: 5, backoff_ms: 200 }
```
Also couple of implementation notes: snapshot only hot prefixes, compress, and tag with request_id.

alex: sounds reasonable. Two questions: how do we ensure idempotency on requeue? and what's the cost hit at 5s snapshot interval?

sam: Requeue idempotency -> assign global request_uuid and use lease tokens: requeued worker checks if snapshot exists for uuid and resumes. Cost: quick rough calc — for 1k concurrent streams each snapshot ~25KB compressed -> ~25MB/sec write -> about 2GB/min -> ~120GB/hr to GCS. Acceptable for peak if we reduce retries. We can also jitter interval per-priority.

jen: We should test on staging with mixed pool (preemptible + on-demand). If keepalive extends only when capacity exists, we bail to on-demand fallback. Also add metric labels: snapshot_success, snapshot_latency, resume_success.

maria: I'll open a short-lived feature flag and PR to implement snapshot writer + resume logic. @jen can you run a chaos job to simulate 50% preemptible reclaim on staging next week? :crossed_fingers:

evict-bot: Scheduled chaos job 'preemptible-drain-staging' created for 2025-05-14T09:00Z by jen.

alex: perf test plan: run 10k simulated streams, measure user-visible drops and requeue counts. If drops drop >80% at <2x GCS bytes, we ship to prod behind a kill-switch.

maria: sweet. I'll post the PR link when ready and tag everyone. Thanks!
